notes.meaning: God calls on those who want to live right and who seek the Lord to look back at their family history. He compares their origins to stones cut from a rock or dug out of a deep pit. Remembering where they came from reminds them that God can make something wonderful out of nothing.

God tells His people to think about Abraham and Sarah, the human parents of their nation. When God first called Abraham, he was just one solitary man without any children. Yet God blessed him and grew his family into a mighty multitude, showing that He can easily rebuild the small group of exiles today.

The Lord promises to comfort Jerusalem and look with tender love on all her broken ruins. He will transform her dry, empty desert into a fruitful paradise like the garden of Eden. Joy, happy songs, and thankful praise will fill her streets again.

The Lord commands His chosen people to pay close attention to His voice. He announces that His law and divine justice will go out into the wider world. This good news will shine like a bright light to guide people of every nation.

God announces that His saving help is on the way and will arrive very soon. His mighty arm will bring fair judgment and rescue to many peoples. Distant lands across the sea will place their hope and trust in His power.

The Lord tells His people to look up at the sky and down at the ground below. The visible heavens will vanish like smoke, the earth will wear out like old clothes, and mortal people will perish just as easily. But God's gift of salvation and His faithful promises will last forever and never fail.

God speaks directly to those who know what is right and have His law written on their hearts. He urges them not to be terrified when human enemies mock them or speak bitter words against them. Because God is on their side, they do not need to let human insults break their spirit.

Those who mock God's people are only mortal and will not last. Just as tiny moths and worms slowly chew through and ruin woolen cloth, human oppressors will soon waste away and perish. But God's righteousness and His rescue will endure through every generation.

The faithful people cry out to the Lord, pleading with His mighty arm to wake up and act with power. They ask Him to do great wonders just as He did in the ancient past. They recall how He shattered 'Rahab' (a poetic name for proud Egypt) and struck down Pharaoh like a sea monster.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars see Rahab and the dragon as ancient poetic symbols for a sea monster of chaos, representing forces that oppose God's good creation.

notes.meaning: The prayer looks back to the miracle of the Red Sea crossing. God dried up the deep waters to make a safe path right across the sea floor for His rescued people. The God who made a way through impossible waters before can easily deliver His people again.

The people whom the Lord rescues will joyfully return home to Jerusalem with singing. Everlasting happiness will rest upon them like a royal crown. All their deep sadness and bitter groaning will turn around and run away forever.

God Himself answers the prayer, declaring that He alone is the One who brings them comfort. He asks why they would ever tremble in fear before frail human beings who are bound to die. Mortal people wither away just like green grass, so they have no power to stand against God.

Living in constant dread of human enemies means forgetting the Lord who made everything. God is the Almighty Creator who spread out the heavens and laid the foundations of the earth. The angry enemy aims to destroy, but his fury is temporary and will soon vanish without a trace.

The captive exiles bowed down in misery will soon be released from their bonds. They will not die in a dark dungeon, and they will not starve for lack of bread. God will step in swiftly to ensure they survive and find their freedom.

The Lord reminds them of His great power by pointing to the sea. He is the God who stirs up the mighty ocean so that its roaring waves crash, and His name is the Lord of Hosts, the Commander of heavenly armies. A God of such boundless strength is fully capable of saving His people.

God explains that He has placed His true words in the mouth of His servant and sheltered him safely in the shadow of His hand. Through this powerful message, God will bring about a new spiritual world, like planting new heavens and a new earth. In this new creation, He will warmly assure Zion that they are His own beloved people.

Jerusalem is told to wake up and get back on her feet. The city had suffered terrible judgment for her sins, pictured as being forced to drink a cup of God's fury until she staggered like a drunkard. She has now drained that bitter cup down to the very last drops, meaning her time of punishment is over.

In the middle of her dizzy suffering, Jerusalem had no one to help her. Not a single one of the sons she had given birth to and raised was able to guide her or take her gently by the hand. Her leaders and citizens were all too weak and overwhelmed to lift her up.

Terrible pairs of disasters struck Jerusalem: her land faced ruin and destruction, while her people faced famine and warfare. Her suffering was so overwhelming that no human being could offer real comfort or fix her deep sorrow. Only the Lord could bring hope to such a hopeless situation.

Jerusalem's young men fainted from hunger and lay helpless at the corners of every street. They were like wild antelopes caught in a hunter's net, completely unable to break free. They were overwhelmed by the heavy discipline and anger of the Lord.

The Lord tells afflicted Jerusalem to listen to what He has to say next. She is stumbling and drunk, but not from drinking too much wine. Her staggering comes entirely from the painful shock and deep sorrow of God's judgment.

The Lord, the God who actively defends and protects His people, delivers wonderful news. He has taken the staggering cup of wrath out of Jerusalem's trembling hands. He promises that she will never have to drink from that cup of fury again.

God promises to place that same cup of judgment into the hands of the cruel enemies who abused His people. Those oppressors had treated the Israelites like dirt, forcing them to lie flat on the ground so soldiers could walk over their backs like a paved street. Now God will turn the tables and bring righteous judgment down on those proud tormentors.
